doc.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995

title: Age, practice and daily routine
summary: Age does not matter, education and practice do, and he practices more than ever now.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And then practice makes perfect is the old saying you know? You practice, you know? You can’t just stay in — age hasn’t really much to do with it. I mean that’s, I’ve had that argument so much in Europe, you know. A lot of people think when you get old you can’t play this or you can’t play that. Age has nothing to do with it whatever. But education has a lot to do with it. You know? Education. Knowing what you’re doing and the next thing important is to know what the other fellow is doing, because you can’t copy if you don’t know what the other fellow is doing also. So that’s the way I keep up. And you have to practice too you know see? Then another thing I think is important, don’t never get to the point that you think you sound so great, you know? You know? Always think there’s more room for improvement. See because in music it’s a science. There’s no such thing as finished. You can always get a better tone. You can always get better ideas. You can always get new harmonies. So many things you can always —as long as you live see? So that, I think that clears your question.
That’s a beautiful answer. Do you have a regular practice routine today?

Yeah, I practice every day around — more so than ever. I’ve been practicing now more so than I ever did in my life. On account of I’m not working as much as I did before. I have time, see, so the spare time that I have I just use the horn to work little things out, you know. Because you can always work them out you know.
